text.p: Following are the main stories from Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:

- A 10-day railway workers' strike has cost the Slovenian economy one billion tolars ($6.47 million) so far. Passenger trains have been running to schedule, while cargo traffic remains partly blocked.
- The Slovenian Chamber of Economy launched a drive to promote Slovenian companies in Greece on Tuesday to increase business cooperation between the two countries.
- Slovenian unemployment fell 0.4 percent to 123,780 in April compared to March and rose 3.2 percent from the same month last year, the Slovenian Employment Office said.
- Only about 60 percent of 35,786 Slovenian companies were profitable in 1996, the Slovenian Payment Agency reported.

- Slovenian ombudsman for human rights Ivan Bizjak on Tuesday presented his report to President Milan Kucan. Although no major violations of human rights were cited, judicial and administrative processes were still too long, Bizjak said.
- Slovenia's second largest bank SKB and UBK bank said on Tuesday they signed a cooperation agreement last week, but declined to give any further details.
